function: Compress and reconstruct optimal continuous RIS phase shifts sent from BS to RIS over a control channel, with an autoencoder and learnable knowledge base (pp. 1-4).
system: Uplink multi-user, one antenna at BS and each UE, passive reflective RIS with 1024 unit cells, no direct path; 28 GHz, 10 MHz (pp. 2, 8).
method: Convolutional autoencoder with shared learnable knowledge base sending only indexes; PSCNet and PSCNet-H (global attention residual blocks); unsupervised reconstruction plus knowledge-base loss (pp. 3-7).
data_channel: SimRIS simulator (Urban Microcell, 28 GHz) generates the channels; 72,000 samples split 60,000 train, 6,000 test, 6,000 validation; optimal phase shift computed from them (pp. 7-8).
test_conditions: Same simulated Urban Microcell data for training and testing (6,000 test samples); compression ratio (1/256 to 1/32) and knowledge-base size varied; no other scenario tested (pp. 8-12).
baselines: Non-learned: OMP [21], AMP [22]; learned CSI-feedback autoencoders: DCRNet [30], CRNet [31], CLNet [32], CsiNet [28] (p. 7).
metrics: NMSE of reconstructed phase shift, average achievable rate, FLOPs and model size, visualized reconstructed phase-shift maps, versus transmitted bits (pp. 8-11).
complexity: FLOPs and model size: PSCNet 0.733 M FLOPs, 11.059 K size at 1/64; PSCNet-H under 1 M FLOPs and 7 K size; benchmarks compared (pp. 9, 11).
q1_support: p. 7: "are generated by the widely used SimRIS channel"; simulator with Urban Microcell channel model at 28 GHz (Table I, p. 8); the paper does not name 3GPP.
q2_support: p. 12: "in varying environmental conditions and with different RIS"; the conclusion leaves this as future work, test samples come from the same simulated data (p. 8), and online fine-tuning is only proposed (p. 5).
q3_support: p. 7: "We provide four deep learning-based methods and two"; non-learned OMP and AMP, and learned DCRNet, CRNet, CLNet, CsiNet, compared on NMSE and rate (Tables II-III, Figs. 6-7).
q4_support: p. 9: "operations (FLOPs) and model size. These metrics represent"; Table IV (p. 9) gives FLOPs and model size for PSCNet and four benchmarks, Table VII (p. 11) for PSCNet-H.
q5_support: p. 8: "A total of 72,000 channel samples were generated, with"; own samples from the SimRIS simulator, with no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Area 3, not 2: the compressed object is the RIS phase-shift vector (the RIS configuration), although the benchmarks are CSI-feedback networks and the phase shift is computed from perfect CSI (p. 3). q1 is marked 1 for the reviewer to confirm: SimRIS with Urban Microcell is named, but 3GPP TR 38.901 is not (p. 7).
